chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim:

Milk, curds, egg, hair, wool, horn, tusk, hoof, and everything that is separated from the beast or the sheep is pure (halal for use), even if you take it from it after it dies; wash it and pray in it.

key_terms.ذَكِيٌّ: Pure/Permissible (in this context, referring to ritual purity and usability)

ai.seo_question: Are animal byproducts like wool and milk pure if taken after the animal dies?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that byproducts like milk, wool, and horns are inherently pure (tahir) because they originate from the living animal, a ruling that extends to them even if retrieved after death without ritual slaughter, provided they are washed. This hadith is central to the Shia juristic distinction between the impurity of the carcass (jutha) and the purity of its excretions and appendages, resolving debates on whether death affects the status of these separated parts. It underscores the practical ease in Islamic law regarding the use of animal-derived materials for clothing and prayer.
